title: feat(app-shell): Studio's validation New menu opens on common rules, with the rule types under Advanced (part of objectui#11861)
body:
Part of #11861 — the validation-rule entry only. The automations and actions entries stay open on the card for later claims.

Clause-②: no

## What changed

Studio's Validations **New** menu opened on the spec's rule types ("Script — CEL fail condition", "Cross-field — CEL over multiple fields", …). It now opens on three plain-language starting points. The per-type list is still there, unchanged, folded under **Advanced**.

| Preset (en / zh) | Spec type | What it writes |
|---|---|---|
| End date on or after start date / 结束日期不早于开始日期 | `cross_field` | It uses the object's first two author `date` fields (or `datetime` fields). The condition is `record.START != null && record.END != null && record.END < record.START` and `fields` is `[END, START]`, so the error attaches to the end date. A message is filled in. **Written at once.** |
| Number can't be negative / 数值不能为负 | `script` | It uses the first author `number` / `currency` / `percent` field. The condition is `record.N != null && record.N < 0` and a message is filled in. **Written at once.** |
| Reject the save when… / 满足条件时拒绝保存… | `script` | The author builds the condition. The rule is **held, not written**, until it has one (objectui#11820), and it opens with the condition editor focused. |

- Each menu row says which fields the preset will use, as its accessible description. For example: Uses “Start Date” and “End Date”.
- If the object lacks the fields a preset needs, the row is **disabled** and says what is missing.
- "Author fields" excludes `system` fields and hidden ones. The audit `created_at` / `updated_at` datetimes are never picked as start and end.
- Every filled condition is a plain `&&` chain that the row builder parses and re-emits byte for byte. A filled preset therefore opens as editable rows, not raw CEL.
- New rules still start on Create + Update.

Files:

- `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/ObjectValidationsPanel.tsx`: the menu, `addPreset`, and a `placeNewRule` shared with `addRule`. It also adds a focusable condition group, which the menu's `onCloseAutoFocus` targets.
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/validationPresets.ts` (new, module-private, not on the package entry): the preset table.
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts`: 12 new rows, en and zh.
- `.changeset/11861-validation-presets.md`: patch for `@object-ui/app-shell`.
- `content/docs/guide/console.md`: the Validations row says what the *New* menu does now (`26f6102`, under the seat's amendment of the claim surface).
- Tests are listed below.

## Mechanism hypotheses, as measured

**H1: the spec already has the shapes. Partly falsified.** I read `@objectstack/spec` 17.7.0, `data/validation.zod.ts`. Its rule types are `script`, `state_machine`, `format`, `cross_field`, `json_schema` and `conditional`. Of the three names on the card:

- **"Date after…"** maps to `cross_field`. It is the spec's own `cross_field` example, and objectstack's showcase `end_after_start` rule has the same shape.
- **"Unique": no spec type.** The spec's validation docblock lists uniqueness under "Deliberately NOT validation rules". A SELECT-then-INSERT check is racy, so the spec points to a unique index or a field's own `unique`. **Left out.**
- **"Required when…" is not offered either.** The spec's validation docblock names this exact phrase as the mis-read it guards against: "Required when X" reads like an invariant and is not one. A `validations[]` rule is an invariant, re-checked against the merged record on every write. "Required when" is a transition gate, which is `Field.requiredWhen`, and the field inspector already offers that as its "Required when" box. A validation preset with this label would steer authors to the wrong tool. The seat ruled option A, so it stays out of this menu.
- In place of those two, I added "Number can't be negative" and "Reject the save when…". The first is the spec's own `script` example, `record.amount < 0`, with a null guard added. The second is the plain-language door to the no-code condition builder.

**The null guard is required, not optional.** objectql evaluates a rule condition fail-CLOSED, so a condition that cannot be evaluated rejects the write. I evaluated through `@objectstack/formula` 17.7.0 `celEngine`:

- On an empty record, `record.end_date < record.start_date` fails with the engine's `no such overload` error: CEL cannot order-compare null.
- On an empty record, `record.amount < 0` fails the same way.
- With the `!= null` guard, both forms answer `{ ok: true, value: false }` on an empty record and `true` on a violation.

That check is now a permanent pin, with a control showing the unguarded form faults.

**H2: one table, not hand-written branches. Confirmed.** `VALIDATION_PRESETS` holds each preset's id, spec type, label key and `plan(fields, locale)`. A preset goes through the same door as a type: `newRule(type)`, then the keys it fills. The focus target is not a separate column. An empty planned condition means "held, focus the condition", so the two cannot disagree. *Advanced* renders the unchanged `RULE_TYPES` list.

**H3: labels, not jargon. Confirmed.** The CEL sits behind the preset, as builder rows in the editor it opens.

## objectui#11820 respected

A preset either fills its condition and is written at once, or it is held until the author gives one. Both paths go through the panel's existing `missingGuard` hold. The pins for objectui#11820 and objectui#9802 (`whenKey`) are green.

⚠️ **The existing pins' menu helpers changed by one line.** `addFromMenu` in `ObjectValidationsPanel.newRuleWaits-11820.test.tsx` and `ObjectValidationsPanel.whenKey.test.tsx`, and two cases in `ObjectValidationsPanel.test.tsx`, now click **Advanced** before clicking the type. That is the navigation this card orders, and it is the only change to those files. No assertion changed.

## Tests

New file: `ObjectValidationsPanel.presets-11861.test.tsx`, 14 tests. It pins:

- **Menu:** the presets come first and number 3 to 5. The type list is folded. Unfolded, it shows the same six types in the same order. It is folded again on every opening.
- **Spec parse, for every preset in the table:** the rule written through `onPatch` parses with the spec's own `ValidationRuleSchema` and `ObjectSchema`, on Create + Update.
- **Exact written rules** for the two filled presets, and confirmation that they open as builder rows.
- **The held preset:** it is not written, the held line shows, and **focus lands on the condition group**. A control checks that a filled preset leaves the menu's normal closing focus on "New".
- **Disabled presets:** each says what it needs, and none takes a `system` or hidden field.
- **Fail-closed safety** through `celEngine`, with the control described above.

Ablations were one-time runs, through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode (anchor must hit; restore proven as blob == HEAD and empty `git diff HEAD`):

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Delete the `onCloseAutoFocus` preventDefault and focus | 1 failed / 13 passed (the focus pin) |
| Delete the number preset's `!= null` guard | 2 failed / 12 passed (the written-rule pin and the celEngine pin) |
| Delete `!f.system &&` from the field filter | 1 failed / 13 passed (the disabled / system-field pin) |

The first attempt at the third row was a no-op. The tool refused it: the replacement string was already inside the anchor, so the count moved by 0. The test command never ran. I re-ran it with a non-overlapping anchor.

NOT MEASURED:

## For the seat

1. **Deviation, i18n prefix.** The claim's surface names new `engine.studio.validations.*` rows. This panel's existing rows all live under `engine.studio.rules.*`, so the new rows use `engine.studio.rules.presets`, `engine.studio.rules.advanced` and `engine.studio.rules.preset.*`, rather than splitting one panel across two prefixes. They are still only new rows, en and zh, in the same file.
2. **Docs (AGENTS.md's docs-driven commandment): done in `26f6102`.** The seat amended the claim surface by the Validations row of `content/docs/guide/console.md`. The row now says that *New* opens on plain-language presets, each writing a working rule or waiting for its condition; that every type is under *Advanced*; that a new rule whose type carries a condition (`script`, `cross_field`, `conditional`) is saved only once it has one; and that a rule's type can still be switched in place.

## Acceptance notes (not filed)

- The panel's message placeholder reads "e.g. Completion date is required when status is Done". That teaches the same "required when" invariant reading the spec warns about. It is not a defect of this change, so I did not touch it. Carrier: none.
- The rule list's type badge still shows the raw type id (`cross_field`, `script`). This is polish outside the New entry. Carrier: none.
